headline: Last session: Sensex rose 300 points as auto stocks gained; market closed for weekend, reopening Tuesday.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Tuesday, 29 September.

why: Auto and consumer durables sectors saw buying interest in the last trading session, gaining nearly 1%.
Markets attempted a recovery after a sharp 1,250-point crash earlier in the week.
Analysts point to geopolitical developments and crude oil as key upcoming market drivers.
Supply constraints in major cities like Mumbai and Delhi-NCR are driving a premium in office rental markets.
whatHappening: A three-day nationwide bank strike is scheduled to begin on September 28, potentially impacting financial services.
Petronet LNG board has approved a commission payment of 1% of profit to its directors.
The Indian stock market has concluded its seventh straight week of losses despite the Friday recovery.
The Indian durables market is projected to reach Rs 3.25 lakh crore by 2030, boosting local manufacturing.
summary: The Sensex gained over 300 points in the last session, led by auto and consumer durables, despite ending the week lower. Markets are currently closed for the weekend and will reopen on Tuesday, September 29. Investors are monitoring a planned bank strike and global geopolitical factors for future direction.
